Modern orientalists have confessed that it is impossible to fix the exact geographical position of Resen and it certainly must be erroneous to identify Resen and Ras-al-Aien, as has been done by Bischoff and Moeller, who, under Gehiagen refer to 'Resen or Ras-al-Aien.' According to Buckingham, 'Gehiagen, which Benjamin reached in two days from Bagdad, would seem to be the Felugia of the present maps

he (Benjamin) did not however conceive this to be Babylon as has been supposed, but took it for Resen of the scripture, which is said to have been a great city, and there are still extensive ruins here, to bear out the supposition.  It was a days journey from hence to the ancient Babel." Asher p. 136 f. 261
